11 # Induced and coinduced topologies
12 
13 In this file we define the induced and coinduced topologies,
14 as well as topology inducing maps, topological embeddings, and quotient maps.
15 
16 ## Main definitions
17 
18 * `TopologicalSpace.induced`: given `f : X → Y` and a topology on `Y`,
19   the induced topology on `X` is the collection of sets
20   that are preimages of some open set in `Y`.
21   This is the coarsest topology that makes `f` continuous.
22 
23 * `TopologicalSpace.coinduced`: given `f : X → Y` and a topology on `X`,
24   the coinduced topology on `Y` is defined such that
25   `s : Set Y` is open if the preimage of `s` is open.
26   This is the finest topology that makes `f` continuous.
27 
28 * `IsInducing`: a map `f : X → Y` is called *inducing*,
29   if the topology on the domain is equal to the induced topology.
30 
31 * `IsEmbedding`: a map `f : X → Y` is an *embedding*,
32   if it is a topology inducing map and it is injective.
33 
34 * `IsOpenEmbedding`: a map `f : X → Y` is an *open embedding*,
35   if it is an embedding and its range is open.
36   An open embedding is an open map.
37 
38 * `IsClosedEmbedding`: a map `f : X → Y` is an *open embedding*,
39   if it is an embedding and its range is open.
40   An open embedding is an open map.
41 
42 * `IsQuotientMap`: a map `f : X → Y` is a *quotient map*,
43   if it is surjective
44   and the topology on the codomain is equal to the coinduced topology.
45 -/
46

52 namespace TopologicalSpace
53 
54 variable {X Y : Type*}
55 
56 /-- Given `f : X → Y` and a topology on `Y`,
57   the induced topology on `X` is the collection of sets
58   that are preimages of some open set in `Y`.
59   This is the coarsest topology that makes `f` continuous. -/
60 @[implicit_reducible]
61 def induced (f : X → Y) (t : TopologicalSpace Y) : TopologicalSpace X where
62   IsOpen s := ∃ t, IsOpen t ∧ f ⁻¹' t = s
63   isOpen_univ := ⟨univ, isOpen_univ, preimage_univ⟩
64   isOpen_inter := by
65     rintro s₁ s₂ ⟨s'₁, hs₁, rfl⟩ ⟨s'₂, hs₂, rfl⟩
66     exact ⟨s'₁ ∩ s'₂, hs₁.inter hs₂, preimage_inter⟩
67   isOpen_sUnion S h := by
68     choose! g hgo hfg using h
69     refine ⟨⋃₀ (g '' S), isOpen_sUnion <| forall_mem_image.2 hgo, ?_⟩
70     rw [preimage_sUnion, biUnion_image, sUnion_eq_biUnion]
71     exact iUnion₂_congr hfg
72 
73 instance _root_.instTopologicalSpaceSubtype {p : X → Prop} [t : TopologicalSpace X] :
74     TopologicalSpace (Subtype p) :=
75   induced (↑) t
76 
77 /-- Given `f : X → Y` and a topology on `X`,
78   the coinduced topology on `Y` is defined such that
79   `s : Set Y` is open if the preimage of `s` is open.
80   This is the finest topology that makes `f` continuous. -/
81 @[implicit_reducible]
82 def coinduced (f : X → Y) (t : TopologicalSpace X) : TopologicalSpace Y where
83   IsOpen s := IsOpen (f ⁻¹' s)
84   isOpen_univ := t.isOpen_univ
85   isOpen_inter _ _ h₁ h₂ := h₁.inter h₂
86   isOpen_sUnion s h := by simpa only [preimage_sUnion] using isOpen_biUnion h
87 
88 end TopologicalSpace
89 
90 namespace Topology
91 variable {X Y : Type*} [tX : TopologicalSpace X] [tY : TopologicalSpace Y]
92 
93 /-- We say that restrictions of the topology on `X` to sets from a family `S`
94 generates the original topology,
95 if either of the following equivalent conditions hold:
96 
97 - a set which is relatively open in each `s ∈ S` is open;
98 - a set which is relatively closed in each `s ∈ S` is closed;
99 - for any topological space `Y`, a function `f : X → Y` is continuous
100   provided that it is continuous on each `s ∈ S`.
101 -/
102 structure IsCoherentWith (S : Set (Set X)) : Prop where
103   isOpen_of_forall_induced (u : Set X) : (∀ s ∈ S, IsOpen ((↑) ⁻¹' u : Set s)) → IsOpen u
104 
105 /-- A function `f : X → Y` between topological spaces is inducing if the topology on `X` is induced
106 by the topology on `Y` through `f`, meaning that a set `s : Set X` is open iff it is the preimage
107 under `f` of some open set `t : Set Y`. -/
108 @[fun_prop, mk_iff]
109 structure IsInducing (f : X → Y) : Prop where
110   /-- The topology on the domain is equal to the induced topology. -/
111   eq_induced : tX = tY.induced f
112 
113 /-- A function between topological spaces is an embedding if it is injective,
114   and for all `s : Set X`, `s` is open iff it is the preimage of an open set. -/
115 @[fun_prop, mk_iff]
116 structure IsEmbedding (f : X → Y) : Prop extends IsInducing f where
117   /-- A topological embedding is injective. -/
118   injective : Function.Injective f
119 
120 /-- An open embedding is an embedding with open range. -/
121 @[fun_prop, mk_iff]
122 structure IsOpenEmbedding (f : X → Y) : Prop extends IsEmbedding f where
123   /-- The range of an open embedding is an open set. -/
124   isOpen_range : IsOpen <| range f
125 
126 /-- A closed embedding is an embedding with closed image. -/
127 @[fun_prop, mk_iff]
128 structure IsClosedEmbedding (f : X → Y) : Prop extends IsEmbedding f where
129   /-- The range of a closed embedding is a closed set. -/
130   isClosed_range : IsClosed <| range f
131 
132 /-- A function between topological spaces is a quotient map if it is surjective,
133   and for all `s : Set Y`, `s` is open iff its preimage is an open set. -/
134 @[fun_prop, mk_iff isQuotientMap_iff']
135 structure IsQuotientMap {X : Type*} {Y : Type*} [tX : TopologicalSpace X] [tY : TopologicalSpace Y]
136     (f : X → Y) : Prop where
137   surjective : Function.Surjective f
138   eq_coinduced : tY = tX.coinduced f
139 
140 end Topology
